summary: Priority lane credit exhaustion causing interleaved chat + embedding 429s
description: Customer reports repeated 429 throttles for interactive chat requests after they enabled high-throughput embedding workers. Symptoms appear when chat traffic (low latency, small payloads) and bulk embedding jobs (large token volumes) run concurrently under the same tenant. The customer uses a dedicated pool with priority lanes configured: 'interactive' and 'batch'. They say interactive requests start receiving 429s intermittently despite quota left in tenant console.
impact: Customer-facing chat experiences intermittent failures during morning embed pipeline runs; multiple downstream users report timeouts and degraded product availability. Business impact: impaired UX for paying customers on dedicated tier.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a dedicated tenant with two priority lanes: interactive (weight 80) and batch (weight 20).
Start ten sustained embedding workers uploading batches of 25k tokens each, with short exponential backoff for retries.
Simultaneously send high-rate interactive chat traffic (50 req/s, median 40 tokens) pinned to 'interactive' route.
Observe 429 responses on interactive requests after ~2-5 minutes while tenant console still shows tenant token credits remaining.
Collect response headers from failed chat requests (e.g., X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After) and relay to Support.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: batch workers' large per-request token accounting is draining the shared burst pool allocated to the tenant's priority lanes faster than the console's tenant-level quota refresh shows, leading to ephemeral 429s on interactive route.

Found rate-limiter code path where per-request accounting for batch route uses a 'bulk_token_multiplier' that multiplies token usage before applying lane-weight smoothing. That multiplier combined with the current smoothing_window=60s caused front-loaded debit of burst credits.

Observed mismatch between 'tenant token balance' displayed in Console (which is refreshed on a 5-minute cadence) and in-memory burst credit counters used by the rate-limiter (which track sub-minute burst pools).

Reproduced locally by issuing a single 25k-token embed request then immediately hammering interactive requests; observed X-RateLimit-Remaining drop to 0 for interactive lane even though console showed ~70% tenant credits remaining.
Correlated incident time with embed pipeline schedule (03:15–03:30 UTC) and increased embed worker concurrency at customer side.
resolution_notes: Applied short-term canary config changes to customer's dedicated pool (approved):
- Set route-level cap for batch route to max_burst_tokens=100000 per-minute (prevents front-loaded multipliers from draining interactive credits).
- Increased interactive lane weight from 80 to 92 for 1-hour canary to prioritize low-latency traffic.
Observed results: interactive 429s stopped within 3 minutes of canary rollout while embed throughput reduced by ~18%. Customer confirmed chat requests succeeded and product UX recovered.

Root cause: combined effect of per-request bulk multiplier + short smoothing window + large embedding batch sizes produced transient exhaustion of priority burst bucket even though tenant-level quota still had headroom.

Permanent next steps agreed: engineering to (1) remove aggressive bulk_token_multiplier for dedicated tenants with priority lanes, (2) add route-level default caps for batch-like routes on dedicated pools, (3) surface burst-pool metrics in Console (per-lane burst credits, per-route burst consumption), (4) document recommended batch sizing for hybrid workloads.
Follow-up task: INT-5402 to implement metrics and INT-5403 to update rate-limiter behavior.
